On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

steps.message:
Analysis: Found the bug! In the load_breach_hashes() function, it uses f.readlines() which preserves the newline characters (\n) at the end of each line. So the breach_set contains hashes like '$2b$12$emdxwc...\n', but the database hashes don't have newlines. This means the comparison 'if pw_hash in breach_set' will always fail. The comment even notes this is a BUG.
Plan: Fix the scan.py script by stripping the newlines from each line when loading breach hashes. I'll use strip() method or read().splitlines() instead. Then run the scanner to verify it works.
